title: Tagged Template Literals
summary: Pass template text and values to a function for custom processing.
nestedConcepts: Pass a template to a tag function
Return the result a caller needs

subtopics.title: Pass a template to a tag function
subtopics.explanation: A tagged template calls a function with the literal string parts and inserted values as separate arguments. For example, a localization tag can place a user name into a translated sentence. The tag decides how to combine or interpret those pieces; the syntax does not automatically escape them.

subtopics.title: Handle inserted values separately
subtopics.explanation: The tag receives values inside `${...}` separately from the surrounding text. This lets it inspect or encode each value for its intended context. For example, a query-building tag can bind values rather than concatenate them into SQL text. Correct safety depends on how the tag handles every insertion.

subtopics.title: Return the result a caller needs
subtopics.explanation: A tag function can return a string, an object, or another value. A CSS-in-JS tag may return a style object, while a localization tag may return translated text. Give the result a clear type and purpose so readers know how the tagged template is used.

subtopics.title: Escape for the output context
subtopics.explanation: Text that is safe in HTML text may not be safe in an HTML attribute, URL, JavaScript string, or SQL query. A tag must use encoding or parameter binding designed for that exact context. Never assume that tagged-template syntax alone prevents injection.

subtopics.title: Review security-sensitive tags
subtopics.explanation: Treat a custom tag as ordinary application code and review how it processes untrusted values. Use a well-maintained library for security-sensitive output, such as HTML sanitization or SQL parameter binding. Test values containing quotes, markup, and unusual characters to confirm they remain data.

foundations.overview: A tagged template is a function call written directly before a template string. JavaScript passes the fixed text pieces and interpolated values separately. A tag can format or validate them, but it must still handle untrusted input safely.
foundations.mentalModel: It is like handing a tailor the fabric pieces and measurements separately.
foundations.whyItMatters: Libraries use tags for formatting, localization, and safe query construction.

keyTakeaways: A tag function receives strings and inserted values.
Interpolated values remain separate from literal text.
Escaping rules depend on the output context.
A tag is not automatically safe from injection.
